title: Compute brief - 19 October 2026
description: Power, not demand, set the weekend's terms. Microsoft exits Nscale's Loughton site after UK Power Networks pushes grid power into the 2030s; NextDC halts ASX trading over a power delay at M3 Melbourne; Anthropic signs a 20-year lease for 95 MW of EverWind's 420 MW Nova Scotia campus. Tape: 69 confirms, 0 ticks, 2 NEW (Crusoe B200 $8.50, B300 $9.90 on-demand).
og_kicker: Grid timing costs the UK its anchor tenant; Anthropic leases in Nova Scotia
lede: The weekend's conversion news was decided by the wire into the building. Microsoft ended its anchor deal at Nscale's Loughton, Essex site, the UK's flagship AI supercomputer project, after UK Power Networks said sufficient power would not arrive until the early to mid 2030s; Microsoft says the decision relates to a single site and Nscale says it is looking for alternative power. In Melbourne, NextDC asked for an ASX trading halt to assess a delay to power supply at its partly built M3 campus, including on FY27 guidance. Where the developer pays for the grid, deals closed: Anthropic signed a lease of at least 20 years for the first 95 MW of EverWind's planned 420 MW Point Tupper campus in Nova Scotia, with EverWind funding all attributable connection and network costs. In silicon, Seoul Economic Daily reported that Nvidia asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to build its custom NVHBM base dies on TSMC 3nm and that Samsung agreed (no company has confirmed), and CXMT guided preliminary Q3 revenue up 589% to 619%. The SOX closed 16 October at 11,137.29 after eight straight losing sessions, its longest streak since 2008, while Cantor said chip-equipment makers are effectively sold out. On the public silicon tape every venue returned HTTP 200: 69 confirms, 0 ticks and 2 NEW rows, as Crusoe's GPU list now shows public on-demand prices for B200 ($8.50) and HGX B300 ($9.90).

countries.note: Microsoft ends its anchor deal at Nscale's Loughton, Essex AI site (about GBP 2 billion, about 23,000 Nvidia GPUs planned) after UK Power Networks put sufficient power in the early to mid 2030s; Nscale exploring alternative power (Wire, 18 Oct).

countries.name: Australia
countries.note: NextDC trading halt over a power supply delay at M3 Melbourne, possible FY27 guidance impact; about 42 MW online in FY2026 and 165 MW under development per Bloomberg; announcement due by 21 Oct (Wire, 19 Oct).

countries.name: Canada
countries.note: Anthropic leases the first 95 MW of EverWind's Point Tupper, Nova Scotia campus for at least 20 years (late 2027), with a 325 MW expansion targeted for 2028; EverWind funds attributable grid costs; more than $10 billion planned including wind (Wire, 16 Oct).
